answer: One workable design: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because wharf only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, voyage is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any signal approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
